title: A finite colimit of finitely presentable objects is finitely presentable
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category whose Hom-sets are small. Call an object $P$ of $\mathcal C$ *finitely presentable* if for every small filtered category $\mathcal I$, every diagram $D:\mathcal I\to\mathcal C$ and every colimit cocone $(L,(c_i)_i)$ of $D$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], the canonical map $\theta_P:\varinjlim_i\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,D(i))\to\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,L)$ (colimit of sets; $\theta_P$ restricted to the $i$-th term is $g\mapsto c_i\circ g$) is bijective, i.e. $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,-)$ preserves filtered colimits. Let $\mathcal K$ be a finite category (finitely many objects and morphisms), $Y:\mathcal K\to\mathcal C$ a diagram with $Y(k)$ finitely presentable for every object $k$, and $(Q,(q_k)_k)$ a colimit cocone of $Y$. Then $Q$ is finitely presentable. In particular: an object isomorphic to a finitely presentable object, a finite coproduct (in an additive category, a finite direct sum) of finitely presentable objects, and, in a preadditive category, a cokernel of a morphism $f:P_1\to P_0$ between finitely presentable objects (a colimit of the diagram $P_1\rightrightarrows P_0$ formed by $f$ and $0$) are finitely presentable.
